questions.a: Special body features or habits that help an organism survive in its surroundings.

questions.q: Give one adaptation of a camel.
questions.a: Stores fat in its hump, drinks and stores much water, and has wide padded feet for sand.

questions.q: Give one adaptation of a fish.
questions.a: Streamlined body and gills to breathe dissolved oxygen in water.

questions.q: Name the two broad habitat types.
questions.a: Terrestrial habitats (land - forests, deserts, mountains) and aquatic habitats (water - ponds, oceans).
The place with air, water, food and shelter where an organism lives.

questions.q: Give one example of an organism and its habitat.
What are biotic components of a habitat?
questions.a: The living parts - plants, animals, microbes around an organism.
Non-living surroundings - air, water, soil, temperature, light.

questions.q: Give one biotic and one abiotic part of a pond.
questions.a: Biotic: fish, algae. Abiotic: water, sunlight, mud.

questions.q: List the characteristics that show something is living.
questions.a: Growth, respiration, nutrition, response to stimuli, excretion and reproduction.

questions.q: Why is a car not called living though it moves and burns fuel?
questions.a: It cannot grow, reproduce or respond by itself - motion alone is not life.

questions.q: Do plants respond to stimuli? Give an example.
questions.a: Yes - mimosa leaves fold on touch; shoots bend toward light.
